newsitem.title: USA: U.S. GFOA opposes securities litigation reform.
newsitem.headline: U.S. GFOA opposes securities litigation reform.

text.p: Over 3,000 Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA) delegates meeting here gave final approval Tuesday to 12 policies, including opposition to some efforts at securities litigation reform.
GFOA's executive board had cleared the policies at a meeting on Monday, following debate by association committees here on Saturday.
Among its policies, the group said it opposes any new litigation and regulation reform efforts in Congress that would preempt state securities laws and limit access to state courts by bond investors.

GFOA also urged the National Association of Securities Dealers to adopt markup rules for the government securities market, including a requirement that dealers disclose markups upon request by investors before final sale.

Another policy calls on muni industry groups to develop procedures for getting important default notices to actual bond holders, known as "beneficial" owners. Because of book-entry registration, many notices currently go only to nominal holders of bonds.
GFOA also said it opposes federal legislation that would relax standards for exchange-traded derivatives and that would create a "professional trading market" for futures.
It also called on governments to remove "artifical restrictions" on the investment of public funds and the use of banking services.
